segments.text: a beaver in a wooden box is falling out of a plane, under a parachute.
The box hits a meadow, pops open, and out he waddles.
Back in a lake town, beavers were felling trees and flooding yards. They had to go.
But horses and mules hauling them got, one game man wrote, spooky and quarrelsome.
So: old war parachutes, and a box that springs open when it lands.
The test pilot: an old beaver called Geronimo. Dropped again, and again, and again.
Until Geronimo started climbing back into the box himself, ready to go again.
That year, {76|seventy-six} beavers flew out. Geronimo among the first, with three females.
A year later: dams, lodges, colonies. And Geronimo had one of his own.
